text:
sre-bot: [PAGER] prefix-cache hit-rate collapse detected for tenant GammaCorp (vpc-uk1). Alerts: prefix_hit_rate_1m down 78% -> 4%, eviction_rate spiked, p95 latency > 2.5s. Affected: dedicated-pool dp-42. See incident: <https://incidents.redwood/INC-4209>

oncall_maria: Ack. I'm on it. Pulling dashboards: https://console.redwood/d/kv/prefix?tenant=GammaCorp

oncall_maria: Quick check: I'm seeing repeated high-rate SET/DEL from an ip we attribute to the customer's batch job (10.8.22.14). Looks like high-cardinality ephemeral keys causing eviction storm.

oncall_maria: Plan (fast mitigation): 1) disable prefix cache for GammaCorp, 2) route traffic gradually to shared fallback pool, 3) notify CS + customer. Executing step 1 now.

eng-runtime-jay: Noted. KV metrics show ~60% of keys with TTL=0 in the last 10m and churn on the LRU list. Strong signal for cache pollution from frequent writes. Suggest per-tenant isolation + small LRU cap as follow-up.

oncall_maria: Executing admin call to disable prefix cache for GammaCorp (canary 100% for tenant).

```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/tenants/GammaCorp/cache/actions" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"action":"disable_prefix_cache","reason":"eviction_storm"}'
```

infra-ops-arnav: I'll start routing change to send new connections to shared-low-latency fallback pool (shared-pool-3). Doing 10% canary now, then 100% if stable.

cs-sam: Notifying GammaCorp CSM and engineering: "We're seeing high latency and transient errors; applying temporary mitigations now. We'll follow up with root cause and post-incident notes." (email + customer Slack sent).

oncall_maria: API responds 200 OK; prefix cache disabled. Observing metrics... eviction_rate dropping.

eng-runtime-jay: Early numbers: eviction_rate down ~92%, prefix hit-rate climbed from 4% -> 58% (isolated cold rebuild). p95 latency down from ~2.9s to ~340ms. Looks promising.

solutions-liz: Coordinating with customer for short-term throttles on their job. Asking them to pause the bulk upsert for 1-2 hours while we stabilise.

oncall_maria: Handing off active work to @eng-runtime-jay (going off shift). Handoff note: monitor alerts for 30m; escalate to L2 if recurrence. Paging remains active. :wave:

eng-runtime-jay: Taking over. I'll roll a per-tenant LRU cap and raise default KV TTL for GammaCorp in dp-42 to prevent repeat. Rolling config change now (no downtime expected).

```
# deploy snippet (internal deploy tool)
deploy service=kv-store pool=dp-42 \n  --set tenant.GammaCorp.max_prefix_keys=50000 \n  --set tenant.GammaCorp.kv_ttl_default=60s \n  --strategy=rolling
```

eng-runtime-jay: Deploy started; performing canary on 2 nodes.

product-kate: Please capture customer impact (duration, error rates) for the post-incident report. CS will decide on credits.

cs-sam: Customer agreed to pause the noisy job for 2 hours and requested 1 hour of service credit. Logged with billing.

eng-runtime-jay: Canary successful, full rollout complete. Current metrics: prefix hit-rate 72%, p95 210ms, eviction rate normalised. No further error spikes.

eng-runtime-jay: Mitigation status: mitigated. Keeping prefix cache disabled and isolated entries TTLed for gradual rebuild for 2 hours; LRU cap in place. Next steps: RCA + runbook updates to detect high-cardinality key patterns earlier and an automated per-tenant throttling playbook.

sre-bot: [MITIGATED] Incident flagged as mitigated by eng-runtime-jay. Follow-up: create RCA doc, update runbook, schedule post-mortem with CS & product. Incident link: <https://incidents.redwood/INC-4209/details> :white_check_mark:
